title: Model Lens: Micro-widgets & Token Flow Chart Specs for Per-Route Performance
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design ticket for a compact, modular 'Model Lens' in Redwood Console that surfaces per-model and per-route performance through micro-widgets and detailed token-flow charts. Goal: give engineers and PMs a focused view for fast incident triage and cost optimization decisions without leaving the route page. Includes interactive chart specs (latency percentiles, throughput, token buckets), a lightweight cost overlay, and rollout-aware annotations.
acceptance_criteria: Micro-widgets implemented as reusable components: latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (req/s), tokens/response, token distribution histogram
Time-series chart supports zoom, aggregation switching (1m/5m/1h), and percentile selection (p50/p75/p95/p99)
Token-flow chart shows stacked token types (prompt, generation, system) and an option to normalize to tokens per-second or tokens per-request
Cost overlay displays estimated USD per 1k tokens and estimated cost delta for batching/quantization suggestions
Rollout annotations render inline (canary start/stop, model switch events) and correlate to spikes/drops in metrics
Accessibility: color palette meets AA contrast and all interactive elements keyboard-focusable and screen-reader labeled
Deliverables: Figma prototype, annotated chart-spec document, developer-ready CSS tokens and component anatomy, example API payload for metrics service
review_comments: PM (Samira): Favor showing p95 as primary SLA metric by default; users asked for p95 > mean in interviews.
Eng (Diego): Need API support for p50/p95/p99 pre-aggregations. Suggested default retention/rollup policy: 1w raw 1m, 1m->5m aggregated for 30d, hourly beyond.
Data (Nina): Warn about cardinality explosion if we show token distribution per-subroute; propose sampling heuristics and an opt-in detailed view.
Design (Maya): We'll show p95 band as filled area behind line, p50 as a thinner line, and p99 as dotted to reduce visual noise.
Accessibility (Rohit): Update color tokens to ensure >4.5:1 contrast for p95 band. Provide texture/line-style alternative for colorblind users.
decisions: Primary latency metric: p95 (default); users can toggle to p50/p99
Default resolution: 1 minute for last 24 hours, with aggregation switcher to 5m/1h for longer ranges
Token-flow default breakdown: prompt / generation / system. We will NOT expose user-level token names to avoid PII leakage.
Cost overlay: estimated gross cost model (tokens * model_rate), not billed-precise. Include a link to billing dashboard for exact numbers.
Rollout annotations: integrate with rollout API to automatically annotate canary periods and model swaps on charts
tradeoffs: Show high-resolution (1m) by default for fastest triage vs increased backend/storage costs — mitigated via retention rollups and on-demand raw retrieval
Token distribution heatmap is powerful but can be noisy for low-volume routes; use a volume threshold and sampling window before rendering
Embedding too many micro-widgets on a small viewport vs discoverability: prioritized 3 top micro-widgets and a collapsible details panel
Rendering many percentile series vs readability: use band + single-line strategy to surface variance without clutter
chart_spec_summary: Latency timeseries: p50 (solid thin #0B5FFF), p95 (solid thick #0A73E6 with translucent band for p50-p95), p99 (dashed #074F9B). X axis: UTC time; Y axis: latency ms, log-scale optional for mixed workloads.
Throughput: area chart stacked per-instance vs total (units: requests/second). Secondary axis on latency chart optional for correlation mode.
Token-flow chart: stacked bar per interval with segments prompt/generation/system. Hover shows absolute tokens, tokens/request, and percent breakdown.
Token distribution: 24h heatmap (hour vs percentile bucket) to surface time-of-day latency skews. Color ramp diverges at SLA threshold.
Histogram: configurable bucket widths (linear/log) for response length distribution; used for detecting tail-heavy outputs that increase cost.
Annotations: event layer for deployments, config changes, throttles, and major errors. Each annotation links to related audit log / PR / incident page.
Interactions: hover tooltips with comparative delta to previous window, click-to-filter route, keyboard accessible legends to toggle series, pinch-to-zoom on mobile prototypes.
Defaults: last 24h view with 1m resolution; quick range presets: 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d. Aggregation fallback for ranges >72h to 5m or 1h depending on retention.
implementation_notes: Frontend: React component set using existing chart library (prefer Recharts-lite custom renderer or Visx if perf issues arise). Provide CSS tokens for gap, padding, and mobile breakpoints.
Backend: metrics API must supply precomputed percentiles and token breakdowns. Endpoint: /v1/route_metrics?route_id=&start=&end=&granularity=
Sampling: when rate < threshold (100 req/s), enable per-request sampling to preserve distribution; above threshold rely on rollups
Rollout integration: annotate via webhook from rollout service; include model_version, rollout_id, fraction, and notes
Telemetry: emit view telemetry for chart interactions to validate usage and justify storage cost for 1m retention
